implementation_notes: There is no API that creates or removes a god object: it is a structural finding, so the work is measurement plus a sequence of moves. Detect by counting, per class, how many distinct types it references and how many methods touch nothing but its own fields — the Siemens process found attributes used by more than a third of a class's methods cannot be extracted into any single responsibility. Then plan: sketch responsibilities as colour groups over the class's internal usage map, extract each group (methods together with the attributes they touch) into its own class, and let the attributes no group claimed fall into a small shared core. Re-run the measurement after each extraction; if a change now needs edits in many classes, that is a shotgun surgery and you have over-split — inline the empty classes back.
pitfalls: Detection tools count size or complexity; a small god object (20 lines, 15 collaborators) passes every threshold and is still the thing everyone routes through.
Extracting fields without the methods that own them produces a shared bag of globals with better folder structure.
The god object re-forms the moment a `Common`/`Utils` module starts accepting the same god object back as a parameter.
